findings.issue: needs-human: Two tabs can restore the same checkpoint. After tab B finishes and removes it, tab A's pagehide unconditionally saves its stale state and resurrects the completed exam; an old tab can also clear a newer exam. A complete fix needs an explicit single-session ownership/takeover policy and atomic cross-tab storage operations (for example Web Locks), including a compatibility decision for contexts without that API. Token checks or storage events alone leave a TOCTOU window.

After a background/frozen page resumes, interval counters can lag wall time. pagehide/visibilitychange then save the old remain/elapsed together with a fresh savedAt, erasing the interruption from subsequent recovery. Countdown and untimed exams must derive elapsed time from a wall-clock anchor before rendering, finishing or saving.

validate accepts non-boolean timed and timed=false with a positive durSec, and skips remain validation for untimed checkpoints. Corrupt data can restore a countdown as an unlimited exam and change modes again on the next save instead of failing safely to setup.

Checkpoint question strings are validated only by type, but resumeExam bypasses buildQuestions' escaping and feeds them to innerHTML in question, choice and result rendering. Raw HTML in stored stem/opts/subj is accepted and can execute handlers. No remote attacker-controlled storage write path was established; reject strings that violate the existing escaped-text checkpoint format.

summary: Fixed three findings with red-to-green regressions: lost elapsed time after suspended timers, inconsistent timer metadata, and unchecked checkpoint HTML; focused Chromium tests pass 13/13. needs-human: stale-tab writes can still resurrect a completed exam, so cross-tab ownership/takeover and atomic-storage compatibility need a decision; fixed=false reflects this unresolved high finding. Full site tests finish 41 passed / 4 pre-existing homepage failures, Python tests pass 137/137, and deployed/default-branch acceptance remains unverified.
